title: The catalog version answer read by rwb-document, its field names and the rwb-document login name are not specified, and the legacy document-to-template key becomes a soft cross-service reference
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 046 Template and merge field catalog as data v1 sections 3, 11 and 12; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (DF-DOC-032 template_id) and T3.3 (document.template_id many to 0 or 1 template); RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 11 and 12.7; context pack P5 ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-11 and R9
description: Legacy RWB-E1-046 keeps the template and merge_field rows in the recovery schema and reads them in process through the TemplateCatalog interface, so the document-to-template relationship is a plain foreign key. In the target the two tables are P6's in rwb_comms, and rwb-document holds only the identifier in document.template_id. No source names the response field that carries that identifier in the catalog answer, no source names the rwb-document login, and no source says how the cross-service reference is kept without a foreign key. The story writes the identifier as a value with no key into rwb_comms and cites this row wherever a name is missing.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.3 lists document.template_id as many to 0 or 1 to template, a foreign key the target cannot hold; RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 12.7 puts template and merge_field in rwb_comms and section 12.1 declares no operation that returns a single version identifier; no source names the per-service login
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad and the P6 rwb-comms squad
proposed: RWB-P6-E1046-CON names the identifier property of the version answer and RWB-PLT-DB fixes the per-service login names before the wave-1 contract tests; the stamp is documented as a soft reference with a reconciliation check instead of a foreign key

title: The dependency rows of this slice name one contract only, and the request field names, the reason field, the index name and the migration step name are not specified
source: Work Package B2-P5-004 story line (H, C, I, X); TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.2 API-P5-006, API-P5-016 and API-P5-017; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07, DP-11, DP-15, DP-19 and R9
description: The Work Package fixes the build row as empty and the contract row as one entry, RWB-P6-E1046-CON, while the pattern set names DP-07 (rwb-case reference-data contract), DP-15 and DP-19 (platform contract stories). The slice therefore consumes the rwb-case list read and the platform libraries without a declared C or H entry. Separately, no source names the request field names of GenerateRequest and RegenerateRequest, the reason field of the regenerate, the error body of a refused document, the index ix_document_template or the Flyway step name, so all of them are placeholders in the story.
evidence: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T-A.2 gives the request classes GenerateRequest and RegenerateRequest by class name only and states the regenerate carries a reason without naming the field; the ownership map and R4 name no index or migration file; the Work Package rows carry one C entry and no H entry
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: The plan adds the rwb-case reference-data contract and the platform contract stories to the dependency rows of this slice, and RWB-P5-E2026-CON names the request fields of the generation and regenerate operations before those stories build

title: The rwb-comms catalog baseline declares no operation that answers the current Approved version for a template code, language and date
source: RWB-P6-E1046-CON sections 7 AC3, 12.1 and 12.2; RWB-E1-046 flow step 6 and AC8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11
description: Legacy RWB-E1-046 publishes TemplateCatalog.current(templateCode, language, onDate), which returns the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid-from date is on or before the date. The rwb-comms baseline declares GET /admin/templates with query code, language, state, page and size, the upload, the content read, the approve and the withdraw, and fixes the current-version rule as a rule but exposes no operation that applies it. The P5 consumer must ask for a resolved current version, including the 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-01 boundary of AC8, and has no operation to call. The fake answers the resolved version and the story records the missing operation.
evidence: RWB-P6-E1046-CON 12.1 lists five operations and none resolves the version in force; its AC3 fixes the catalog version rule and AC7 fixes the state rules as contract elements, so the rule exists without an operation; RWB-E1-046 section 12 names the current-version method
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-comms, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: RWB-P6-E1046-APP adds a resolved current-version read, for example GET /admin/templates/current with code, language and onDate, and RWB-P6-E1046-CON records it as an additive change within major version 1 before the wave-1 contract tests

title: This slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion while the Work Package lists all nine legacy test cases for it
source: Work Package B2-P5-004 story line (acs empty, tcs_legacy of nine IDs, secondary true); split plan entry RWB-P5-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1046-APP; RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 7 closing note
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria; 16 Test cases; 18 Traceability
description: The split gives RWB-P6-E1046-APP all eight legacy acceptance criteria and gives this P5 slice none, while the Work Package hands the same nine legacy test case IDs to every slice of the key. The story therefore writes nine new criteria under D-RCV-60 for the P5 binding, lists the nine legacy test cases with the P5 part of each named in the Covers column, and states that the legacy criteria stay with P6. A reader or a traceability tool that expects every listed test case to cite a legacy criterion owned by the same story sees a mismatch.
evidence: RWB-P6-E1046-CON section 7 closing note states that legacy AC1 to AC8 are owned by RWB-P6-E1046-APP; the plan entry for RWB-P5-E1046-APP has an empty acs list and the same nine tcs_legacy entries as the P6 stories
owner_role: Solution architect, with the traceability owner
proposed: The split plan records one owning story per legacy criterion and marks a secondary slice as test-case-bearing but criterion-free, so the traceability reports do not expect the two lists to match in every slice
